newsitem.title: UK: UK approves 843 MW of renewable energy projects.
newsitem.headline: UK approves 843 MW of renewable energy projects.

text.p: The government said on Thursday it had approved 195 projects to generate a total of 843 MW of electricty from renewable sources of energy under its fourth Non-Fossil Fuel Obligation Order, NFFO-4.
Junior trade and industry minister Richard Page said companies competing for government subsidies under the programme had submitted impressive bids.
He said the average production price for the NFFO-4 projects, covering the period 1997-2016, was 3.46 pence per kilowatt hour, almost one penny better than the 4.35 pence achieved in NFFO-3.
"Real convergence with market prices is clearly now within reach and our strategy of stimulating a competitive renewables market is working well," Page said in a written parliamentary answer.
As a result, he had been able to approve more contracts than he envisaged when NFFO-4 was announced in November 1995.
The government's goal is to work toward 1,500 MW of new renewables-based generation capacity by 2000. Over 428 MW of capacity is already on stream as a result of NFFOs 1-3.
Page said policy would be reviewed prior to NFFO-5 in 1998.

"Over the next few years I expect increasing numbers of renewable energy projects to be developed and be able to generate in the liberalised electrticty market without needing support under the NFFO arrangements," Page said.
